 ORDER Respondent in Crl.Misc.No.177 of 2022 on the file of the Family Court, at Raichur (hereinafter referred to as 'the Trial Court' for brevity), is impugning the order dated 17.05.2023, partly allowing the petition filed under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. and awarding monthly maintenance of Rs.10,000/- to be paid by the respondent in favour of the petitioner and to pay cost of Rs.10,000/-.

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status and rank before the Trial Court.

3. Brief facts of the case are that, the respondent herein as petitioner filed Crl.Misc.No.177 of 2022 under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. contending that she had married the respondent on 14.02.2020 at Raichur and dowry has been paid both in cash as well as in kind.
After marriage, she went to her matrimonial house and was residing with the husband, his mother, father and the sister.

After few days, respondent and his family members started ill-treating her and also demanding NC:
2023:KHC-K:8511 dowry.
Since she could not tolerate the cruelty meted to her, she went to her parental house.
Thereafter, she came to know that the respondent contacted second marriage with one Nagamma on 02.07.2022 and started leading matrimonial life.
Thus, the respondent has deserted the petitioner and neglected to maintain her.
The respondent is doing business and earning morethan Rs.1,00,000/- He has having 20 acres of land in Devasugur village and earning Rs.20 to Rs.30 lakhs per annum.
Therefore, he is in a position to pay maintenance.
Accordingly, she prayed for allowing the petition by granting maintenance of Rs.15,000/- per month.
4. Respondent has appeared before the Trial Court and has filed his objection denying the contention of the petitioner.
It is admitted that they are married on 14.02.2020 and denied that any dowry was either paid or received.
The contention regarding cruelty meted to the petitioner either by respondent or his family members by demanding additional dowry are also denied.
It is contended that the petitioner had left the matrimonial house without intimating him and his family members along with gold ornaments and her other NC: 2023:KHC-K:8511 belongings.
The petitioner is a skilled tailor earning Rs.20,000/- per month and she is capable of maintaining herself.
She is residing in her parental house at Mumbai and deserted the respondent.
The respondent is not having any avocation nor any income.
The respondent has filed MC No.141 of 2021 before the Family Court at Raichur, seeking relief of restitution of conjugal rights.

Therefore,
he prays for dismissal of the petition with costs.

sentences.text: The petitioner examined herself as PW1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P11.
The respondent examined himself as RW1 and got marked Exs.R1 to R4 in support of his defence.

The Trial Court after taking into consideration all these materials on record, allowed the petition filed under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. awarding monthly maintenance of Rs.10,000/- from the date of petition till the end of her life with cost of Rs.10,000/-.
6. Being aggrieved by the same, the respondent is before this Court.
Heard Sri Basavaraj R Math, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri B K Hiremath, learned counsel for the respondent.
Perused the materials on record.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the wife has willfully deserted the respondent immediately after the marriage and started residing in Mumbai.
Ex. R3 - the legal notice dated 20.10.2021 was got issued on behalf of the petitioner-wife from the advocate at Mumbai.
In the said notice, it is specifically stated that the wife is residing at Mumbai.
MC No.141 of 2021 was filed by the respondent before the Family Court, Raichur seeking restitution of conjugal rights.
In spite of service of notice, the petitioner remained absent.
The said petition came to be allowed on 13.04.2022.
Even thereafter, the petitioner has not joined the respondent in the matrimonial house.
There is no refusal to maintain the wife by the respondent.
Under such circumstances, she is not entitled for any maintenance and prays for allowing the petition and to dismiss the claim of the petitioner for maintenance.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent opposing the petition submitted that MC No.141 of 2021 was filed and proceeded without notice to the petitioner.
Therefore, she filed criminal miscellaneous case and granting of restitution of conjugal rights was set aside.
Now the matter is pending for evidence of the petitioner-wife.
Learned counsel also submitted that the respondent has contacted second marriage and therefore, the petitioner is not ready and willing to join him in the matrimonial house.
The respondent is owning 6.29 acres of irrigated land and he is having huge income from the same.
Therefore, there are no reasons to interfere with the impugned order passed by the Trial Court.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petition.

10. In view of the rival contentions urged by learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner has made out any grounds to allow the petition filed by him?"

My answer to the above point is in the 'Affirmative' for the following:

sentences.text: It is the contention of the petitioner that she had married the respondent on 14.02.2020 and had led marital life.
Since she was ill-treated by the respondent and his family members, she left the matrimonial house and started to reside in her parental house.
In the mean time, the respondent contacted second marriage with one Nagamma and started to led marital life.
Therefore, she filed a petition before the Trial Court seeking maintenance.

12. On the other hand, it is the contention of the respondent that even though the petitioner married the respondent on 14.02.2020, she wilfully deserted him within a day and stared residing at Mumbai.
There was no occasion for ill-treating the petitioner.
Even though M.C.No.141 of 2021 was filed before the Family Court at Raichur seeking restitution of conjugal rights, the same was came to be allowed.
The petitioner had not joined the respondent.
Therefore, she is not entitled for any maintenance.

13. It is pertinent to note that the respondent has produced Ex.R1, which is the order passed in M.C.No.141 of NC: 2023:KHC-K:8511 2021, on the file of the learned Principal Judge, Family Court at Raichur, allowing the petition filed under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, directing the respondent therein, who is the petitioner herein to join the company of her husband to lead marital life.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Court at Raichur
entities.label: JUDGE

sentences.text: Even though a specific defence was taken by the petitioner that the said order granting restitution of conjugal rights was set aside, no scrap of paper is produced before this Court to substantiate the said contention.

The learned counsel for the respondent was granted time to produce the copy of the order said to have been passed setting aside the decree for restitution of conjugal rights passed against the respondent.
Till today the said order is not produced.

Therefore,
the contention of the respondent regarding granting of decree for restitution of conjugal rights will have to be accepted.
R2 is the order sheet of the Trial Court in M.C.No.141 of 2021.
According to which, the petitioner had remained exparte in spite of service of notice.

Ex.R3 is the notice dated 26.10.2021,
issued on behalf of the petitioner to the respondent from her advocate at Navi Mumbai.

The NC:
2023:KHC-K:8511 address of the petitioner is shown as the resident of Mumbai.

For which, the respondent has issued reply as per Ex.R4.
15.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P10, the FIR in Crime No.56 of 2022 of Raichur Women police station, for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 323, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, committed between 14.02.2020 till 02.07.2022.
It is pertinent to note that the petition before the Trial Court was filed on 02.09.2022.
Under such circumstances, much importance cannot be given to Ex.P10, which was filed just before filing of the petition, may be to have a cause of action for seeking maintenance.
16. Even though the respondent was cross-examined at length, nothing has been elicited from his evidence to disbelieve his version that the petitioner has voluntarily deserted his company.

When the petitioner failed to probablise her contention that the order dated 13.04.2022 passed in M.C.No.141 of 2021, passed by the Family Court granting a decree for restitution of conjugal rights was set aside by the competent Court and when admittedly the petitioner has not Suresh Pujari vs Rajeshwari @ Vidhya Shree on 8 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183648694/
4 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8511 complied with the directions made therein by jointing the respondent to lead marital life, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not having any justification to live separately and to seek maintenance from the respondent.

entities.text: Suresh Pujari vs Rajeshwari @ Vidhya Shree
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has not made out any ground for seeking maintenance from the respondent.
17. I have gone through the impugned order passed by the Trial Court.

It has taken into consideration the contention taken by the petitioner and proceeded to allow the petition holding that the order passed in M.C.No.141 of 2021 granting decree for restitution of conjugal rights was taken behind the back of the petitioner.
The materials on record discloses that the notice with petition copy of M.C.No.141 of 2021 was served on the wife and she remained exparte.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be concluded by saying that the decree was obtained behind the back of the wife.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the impugned order awarding maintenance of Rs.10,000/- per month is liable to be set aside.

18. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
- 11 -  NC: 2023:KHC-K:8511  ORDER  (i) The petition is allowed.
(ii) The order dated 17.05.2023 passed in Crl.Misc.No.177 of 2022, on the file of the learned Principal Judge, Family Court at Raichur, is hereby set aside.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Court at Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As a result, Crl.Misc.No.177 of 2022 filed under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. is dismissed.
Registry to send back the Trial Court records along with copy of this order.
